title: The Must in the Ticket
subtitle: Cross three places and reconstruct the rule
opening: 08:43. Three connected places remain open, but their machines remember different parts of BUG-4821. No report contains the replay address.

incident-control-room.name: Incident Control / 08:43
incident-control-room.title: The report arrived before the rule.
incident-control-room.instruction: Click a machine to walk to it and inspect. Drag the room to look around; WASD and immersive mouse-look remain optional.

stations.label: Red folder
stations.description: A red incident folder lies open beside an accepted order receipt.
stations.inspect_text: BUG-4821 reports a returned laptop sold before inspection. MUST is circled, but the page names neither source nor owner.

stations.label: Sealed replay surface
stations.description: A black event surface waits behind a keypad. Its plate reads SUBJECT / WINDOW / MACHINE.
stations.locked_text: REPORT IDENTIFIER REJECTED. Assemble independent witnesses from the warehouse, quality record, and customer commitment machines.

stations.label: Dark socket
stations.description: Three green lamps feed the projector; an unwired socket remains dark.
stations.locked_text: The rack flickers without a confirmed deterministic replay trace.

stations.label: Commitment printer
stations.clue: a receipt pulse behind smoked glass
stations.description: A customer-facing terminal remembers when an availability signal became an accepted order.
stations.inspect_text: The terminal reads ORD-99114 without treating it as the execution subject. A strip emerges: WINDOW 09:17 / MACHINE R4.

policy-archive.name: Policy Archive / Below Records
policy-archive.title: A source can support a rule without accepting it.
policy-archive.instruction: Walk the broken circle. Each machine owns one kind of evidence; no glowing edge owns its authority.

stations.label: Quality record index
stations.clue: two missing digits under cold glass
stations.description: The quality archive can locate the awaiting-inspection record, but its subject mask is incomplete.
stations.inspect_text: The index confirms AWAITING_INSPECTION and exposes a masked subject strip: LP-··41. It supports identity and state, not sellability.

stations.label: Open catalogue
stations.description: The catalogue indexes policy by the origin of the unit, its material domain, and the promise the organization is trying to make.
stations.locked_text: A narrow reader waits for a fault classification before it will expose the three index drums.

stations.label: Brass rings
stations.description: Five meanings have been forced onto a single rotating axle.
stations.locked_text: The mechanism has no reference point; a bounded policy fragment may anchor it.

stations.label: Socket console
stations.description: A relation projector has sockets for evidence the glowing edge does not carry by itself.
stations.locked_text: The projector cannot distinguish its endpoints while the brass meanings remain collapsed.

stations.label: Pneumatic terminal
stations.clue: the tube has one empty carrier
stations.description: A review tube accepts one source-bound candidate package.
stations.use_text: SIMULATED OWNER RESPONSE: accepted for CUSTOMER_RETURN / ELECTRONICS. The seal governs bounded organizational use; it does not manufacture physical truth.

transfer-annex.name: Transfer Annex / Chain of Custody
transfer-annex.title: Movement changed the facts, but no source says how.
transfer-annex.instruction: Follow intake, inspection, and release as separate custody zones. Preserve what the broken clock cannot answer.

stations.label: Intake scanner
stations.clue: a split serial beneath the frost
stations.description: The intake scanner knows which physical unit crossed the warehouse threshold, but not why it was offered for sale.
stations.inspect_text: The scanner replays the physical intake and prints a masked subject strip: LP-20··. Presence is witnessed; sellability is not.

stations.label: Transferred crate
stations.description: An inspected return changed warehouses. The chain-of-custody clock stopped during transfer.
stations.locked_text: The crate has a bounded decision, but no way to record what the sources do not answer.

stations.label: Light table
stations.description: Old inspection evidence and a new warehouse tag overlap on the glass.
stations.inspect_text: The old inspection is real evidence. The transfer is also real. Neither fact proves whether clearance survived the move.

stations.label: Seven sockets
stations.clue: the final socket is not a shortcut
stations.description: Seven unlabeled sockets surround a recessed red override.

bug-ticket.name: BUG-4821 ticket
bug-ticket.description: Evidence of an undesirable outcome and an expectation. Not policy authority.

order-receipt.name: ORD-99114 receipt
order-receipt.description: Evidence that the availability signal invited a customer commitment.

warehouse-witness.name: Warehouse witness
warehouse-witness.description: Masked subject strip from physical intake: LP-20··.

quality-witness.name: Quality witness
quality-witness.description: Masked subject strip and state from the quality index: LP-··41 / AWAITING_INSPECTION.

storefront-witness.name: Storefront witness
storefront-witness.description: Commitment window and machine checksum: 09:17 / R4.

event-trace.name: Deterministic event trace
event-trace.description: The pipeline replayed in order and produced the same result.

fault-record.name: FAULT-4821 record
fault-record.description: Semantic-rule gap supported; code defect and policy change unresolved.

policy-fragment.name: Returns-policy fragment
policy-fragment.description: A source supporting inspection before returned electronics enter saleable stock.

semantic-map.name: Separated meaning map
semantic-map.description: Presence, stock, allocation, sellability, and customer signal are distinct.

forbidden-card.name: Forbidden-inference card
forbidden-card.description: Warehouse presence does not imply quality clearance or sellability.

candidate-relation.name: Candidate relation
candidate-relation.description: QualityClearance constrains Sellability, with source, scope, owner, and limits attached.

residue-marker.name: Residue marker
residue-marker.description: Marks a question unresolved and blocks unsafe downstream use.

owner-seal.name: Bounded owner seal
owner-seal.description: Simulated acceptance for returned electronics only.

residue-record.name: Transfer residue record
residue-record.description: Warehouse-transfer inspection validity remains unresolved; sellability is blocked.

runtime-receipt.name: Runtime replay receipt
runtime-receipt.description: Contract, projection, and original fixture replay passed within the bounded case.

archive-coordinate.title: Locate the governing drawer
archive-coordinate.prompt: The fault record gives no drawer number. Tune ORIGIN, DOMAIN, and PROMISE to the coordinate implied by the incident.
archive-coordinate.success: A single drawer releases. The card supports inspection before returned electronics enter saleable stock and routes interpretation to the resale-policy owner.
archive-coordinate.failure: The chosen drawer contains a neighboring rule. Re-read what happened to the unit, what it is, and which organizational promise the ticket is actually challenging.
hints: The unit did not begin as new stock, and transfer is not its original disposition.
A laptop belongs to the policy's electronics domain.
The archive distinguishes physical presence from the state in which a unit may be sold.

ledger-replay.title: Wake the Event Ledger
ledger-replay.prompt: Assemble the Replay Address from the three machine witnesses. Once accepted, capture the five causal signals and prove that the stream survives a browser reboot.
ledger-replay.success: Two captures on opposite sides of a browser reboot match. Duplicate, ordering, stale-cache, and projection-nondeterminism explanations lose their alibis.
ledger-replay.failure: The captured stream does not reconstruct the causal path. The ledger purges the run but preserves the machine address.
hints: Overlay LP-20·· with LP-··41; the customer machine contributes the window and checksum.
The return exists before the warehouse scan; the customer-facing cache changes last.
One correct capture is not enough. Let the browser forget the frame while autosave preserves the machine state.

missing-input.title: Find the absent fact
missing-input.prompt: Connect the one fact the implemented availability rule never declared as an input.
missing-input.success: Quality was not dropped in transit; it was absent from the model. FAULT-4821 is recorded as a semantic-rule gap.
missing-input.failure: That input is already wired into the green decision lamps. Look for the domain fact that never reaches the rack.
hints: Three lamps already correspond to presence, reservation, and sales-channel enablement.
The quality service knew the unit was awaiting inspection.
Connect quality_state to the dark socket.

meaning-chain.title: Uncollapse AVAILABLE
meaning-chain.prompt: Arrange the meanings from physical fact to customer-facing claim.
meaning-chain.success: The five meanings separate. Similar labels no longer collapse distinct domain judgments.
meaning-chain.failure: The rings still make a downstream promise imply an upstream physical fact. Follow the direction from warehouse observation to customer invitation.
hints: Start with what a warehouse can directly observe.
Allocation comes after stock counting but before sellability.
The storefront offer is the final customer-facing claim.

relation-frame.title: Frame the candidate relation
relation-frame.prompt: Place the correct artifacts into SOURCE, SCOPE, OWNER, MEANING, and LIMIT sockets.
relation-frame.success: The line can now travel with provenance and limits. It remains candidate until its named owner decides.
relation-frame.failure: The projector rejects the frame. A graph edge needs more than plausible endpoints.
hints: Every socket names a different kind of support; inspect your artifact descriptions.
The owner route is not the policy source, and the scope card is not the meaning map.
Use the policy, scope, owner, separated map, and forbidden-inference artifacts once each.

transfer-residue.title: The question no source answers
transfer-residue.prompt: The unit moved warehouses after inspection. Use the artifact that preserves uncertainty without inventing a rule.
transfer-residue.success: The missing answer remains visible. Transferred returned units are blocked from sellability until the owner resolves the question.
transfer-residue.failure: That artifact cannot answer the transfer question. No available source supports YES or NO.
hints: The correct move does not decide whether inspection remains valid.
A visible hole is safer than an invented rule.
Use the residue marker on the unresolved transfer case.

evidence-chain.title: Build the exit chain
evidence-chain.prompt: Insert the seven records in the order that lets evidence become bounded construction.
evidence-chain.success: The original fixture replays: awaiting inspection stays unavailable; passed inspection becomes sellable. The transfer residue remains attached. Door released.
evidence-chain.failure: The chain overclaims one layer. Evidence must precede interpretation, authority must precede the contract, and runtime proof comes last.
hints: Begin with the report, then prove what the running system did.
The owner seal comes after the candidate relation and before implementation contract.
BUG → TRACE → FAULT → RELATION → OWNER → CONTRACT → RUNTIME.

false-green.title: False green
false-green.summary: The override opened a service hatch, not the safe exit. The fixture passed while an unconfirmed rule impersonated authority.

honest-construction.title: Incident room released
honest-construction.summary: Evidence, meaning, owner commitment, construction, runtime proof, and unresolved residue survived as distinct records.
